Alert.description:
Keeps users informed of important and sometimes time-sensitive changes.

Important Notes:
- The `intent` prop uses "information" (not "info") for the blue
  informational style
- Default intent is "neutral" - only set intent when you need a specific
  color/emphasis

AlertDialog.description:
Display a modal with important content that expects confirmation from the
user.

AlertDialog does NOT have a close (X) button in the header - users must
explicitly choose an action. This is intentional for confirmation dialogs to
prevent accidental dismissal of critical actions.

Use for confirmations, destructive actions, and critical decisions. Do not
use for general forms or informational content (use Dialog instead).

For async operations, use event.preventDefault() in AlertDialogAction onClick
to prevent auto-close, then manually close after completion.
AlertDialog.name: AlertDialog

defaultOpen.description: The initial open state in uncontrolled mode.

onOpenChange.description: Handler that is called when the open state changes.

open.description: The open state in controlled mode.

examples.title: async-usage
examples.description:
We can prevent closing the dialog in the action button's `onClick` handler to perform async operations.

Make sure to use the controlled props and call `event.preventDefault()` in your action to stop the modal from being dismissed.
examples.heading: Handling async events

examples.title: confirmation-usage
examples.description: Add an `onClick` handler to `AlertDialogAction` to perform an action on confirmation.
examples.heading: Handling confirmation

examples.title: controlled-usage
examples.description: Use the `open` and `defaultOpen` props to toggle between controlled and uncontrolled usage. And combine it with `onOpenChange` to listen for changes to the state.
examples.heading: Controlled

examples.title: managed-confirm-usage
examples.description: We can also use the `await dialogkit.confirm()` shortcut method to show an alert dialog and get a boolean result based on whether the user confirms or cancels the dialog.
examples.heading: Managed ALPHA

examples.title: managed-usage
examples.description: Use `dialogkit.create()` to create alert dialogs in managed mode. In managed mode you must omit the `AlertDialog` element and only send the `AlertDialogContent` element and its children.
examples.heading: Managed ALPHA

examples.title: size-usage
examples.description: Use the `size` prop to change the size of the dialog box.
examples.heading: Sizes

examples.title: trigger-usage
examples.description:
By default we use the `Button` component for the dialog trigger which accepts all of the existing button props.

We can also completely change the trigger by using `asChild` and passing our own component.
examples.heading: Customize trigger

import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogBody,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger>Delete comment</AlertDialogTrigger>

      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>Delete comment?</AlertDialogHeader>

        <AlertDialogBody>
          The comment and all replies will be deleted.
        </AlertDialogBody>

        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel />
          <AlertDialogAction>Yes, delete</AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}

AlertDialog.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space`, `Enter` | When focus is on `AlertDialogTrigger`, opens the dialog. |
| `Esc` | Closes the dialog and moves focus to `AlertDialogTrigger`. |

- md (600px): Moderate content, longer messages, 2-3 actions
- lg (800px): Detailed alerts with longer descriptions or more context

💡 Tip: When matching designs from screenshots, compare the content
density and action count against these guidelines. Most alerts work well
at 'sm' (default) and only need to increase if the design clearly shows
more content.

AvatarGroup.description:
Displays a group of avatars representing multiple users with automatic layout
and overflow handling.

Use this component whenever you have 2 or more Avatar components together,
even if they're not overlapping in the design. AvatarGroup handles consistent
sizing, spacing, overflow indicators (+N), and semantic grouping
automatically.

Don't manually layout multiple Avatars in a Flex - use AvatarGroup instead.

When to use:
- Multiple assignees on a task
- Team members or collaborators
- Participants in a conversation
- Any group of users
AvatarGroup.name: AvatarGroup

A primitive layout component that provides access to design tokens and
styling without custom CSS.

Use Box for simple styling (padding, margin, colors, borders) when you
don't need flexbox layout features. For flexbox layouts with
direction/alignment/gap, use Group instead.

Use `extractBoxProps` to separate sprinkle props from the rest when
rendering non-div elements with `asChild`.

Button.description:
Button component for triggering actions, with support for icons, addons, and
loading states.

Use this for standard action buttons. The component supports icon-only
buttons, buttons with leading/trailing icons, and custom addon content before
or after the main label.

When not to use:
- For menu and select buttons with a chevron use AngleMenuButton instead.
- For ellipsis menus use EllipsisMenuButton instead.
- For buttons that include label use LabelMenuButton instead.
- For expand/collapse triggers use Disclosure instead of Button with chevron
  icon and manual state.
- Don't use Button to build tab navigation - use Tabs instead.
Button.name: Button

examples.title: disabled-usage
examples.description:
Set the `disabled` prop to `true` to disable buttons and prevent any interactions.

Include visible text that explains why it's disabled: a disabled button leaves the tab order, so keyboard and screen reader users can't reach a tooltip on it.
examples.heading: Disabled state

examples.heading: File upload

examples.title: group-usage

examples.heading: Grouping buttons

examples.title: icon-only-usage
examples.description:
Use the `icon` prop and omit the `children` to display an icon only button.

For accessibility please make sure to always include an `aria-label` prop for screen readers and optionally use tooltips to visually denote the button's intent.
examples.heading: Icons > Icon only button

examples.title: icon-usage
examples.description: Icons are placed to the left by default but can be placed to the right using the `iconPosition` prop.
examples.heading: Icons > Left and right icons

examples.title: link-disabled-usage
examples.description:
Make sure to prevent interactions manually using `event.preventDefault()` since `<a>` elements do not support the `disabled` prop.

Alternatively you can use our `Link` component which supports the `disabled` prop.
examples.heading: Links > Disabled button links

examples.title: link-usage
examples.description: Set `asChild` to `true` and wrap children in an `<a>` element to render buttons as links.
examples.heading: Links > Button as links

examples.title: loading-usage
examples.description:
Set the `loading` prop to `true` to show a loading spinner and mark the button `aria-busy`.

Don't also set `disabled`: a disabled button loses keyboard focus mid-action. The button stays clickable while loading, so ignore repeat clicks in your `onClick` handler if the action shouldn't run twice.
examples.heading: Loading state

Button.accessibility:
### Labels

- Give an icon only button an `aria-label`, since it has no visible text. Button logs a console error when the label is missing.
- A disabled button leaves the tab order, so keyboard and screen reader users can't reach a tooltip on it. Explain why it's disabled in visible text nearby.

### Loading

`loading` marks the button `aria-busy` and keeps it focusable and clickable. Ignore repeat clicks in your handler when the action shouldn't run twice.

import { IconMusic, IconStar } from "@optiaxiom/icons";
import {
  Badge,
  Box,
  Button,
  Card,
  CardAction,
  CardCheckbox,
  CardHeader,
  CardPreview,
  Group,
} from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Group flexDirection={["column", "row"]} gap="16">
      <Card size="224">
        <CardPreview
          addonTopLeft={
            <CardAction>
              <CardCheckbox />
            </CardAction>
          }
          bg="bg.page"
          flex="1"
        >
          <Box
            bg="bg.default"
            color="fg.success"
            p="16"
            rounded="md"
            shadow="sm"
          >
            <IconMusic size="32" />
          </Box>
        </CardPreview>
        <CardHeader>Checkbox</CardHeader>
      </Card>
      <Card size="224">
        <CardPreview
          addonBottomLeft={<Badge intent="warning">Duplicate</Badge>}
          addonTopLeft={
            <CardAction>
              <CardCheckbox />
            </CardAction>
          }
          addonTopRight={
            <CardAction>
              <Button aria-label="Add to favorites" icon={<IconStar />} />
            </CardAction>
          }
          bg="bg.page"
          flex="1"
        >
          <Box
            bg="bg.default"
            color="fg.success"
            p="16"
            rounded="md"
            shadow="sm"
          >
            <IconMusic size="32" />
          </Box>
        </CardPreview>
        <CardHeader>Checkbox and star button</CardHeader>
      </Card>
    </Group>
  );
}

Checkbox.description:
Basic control to allow selecting one or more items from a set.

Important Notes:
- The control and its focus ring reach up to 6px outside the checkbox, so a
  scroll container (`overflow="auto"`) clips them on its edge rows. Pad the
  scroll container by at least 6px (`p="8"`); to keep the checkboxes flush
  with the content around it, cancel the padding with an equal negative
  margin.

Checkbox.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space` | Toggles the checkbox between checked and unchecked |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to or away from the checkbox |
| `Shift + Tab` | Moves focus to the previous focusable element |

Checkbox automatically handles accessibility:

- Uses proper `role="checkbox"` and ARIA attributes
- Supports `aria-checked` for checked/unchecked/indeterminate states
- Associates label text with the checkbox control

examples.title: empty-usage
examples.description: Use the `empty` prop on `DataTableBody` to show content in a full-width row when the table has no rows.
examples.heading: Empty state

examples.title: expanding-rows-usage
examples.description:
Follow the expanding guide to allow expanding and collapsing rows.

Use the `DataTableExpandableHeader` and `DataTableExpandableCell` components to render columns with built-in buttons for toggling rows.

Finally, combine it with the `loading` prop to show a loading state while expanded rows are being fetched.
examples.heading: Expanding rows ALPHA

examples.title: list-view-usage
examples.description: A collection page combines a search input and filter menus above the table with a primary create action. Wire search to `globalFilter` and each menu to its column's filter value, add `getFilteredRowModel` and `getPaginationRowModel`, and TanStack resets to the first page whenever the criteria change. Put row commands in a trailing column behind one `EllipsisMenuButton`, and use `empty` to offer a way out when nothing matches.
examples.heading: List view

examples.title: loading-row-usage
examples.description: Alternatively you can provide an object to the `loading` prop to denote individual loading state of sub rows.
examples.heading: Loading state

examples.title: loading-usage
examples.description: Set the `loading` prop to `true` to show a loading skeleton while your table data is loading.
examples.heading: Loading state

examples.title: pagination-client-usage
examples.description: Simply provide the `getPaginationRowModel` and `pagination` options to use client-side pagination.
examples.heading: Pagination > Client side

examples.title: pagination-server-usage
examples.description: To implement manual server-side pagination we can use `manualPagination` and `rowCount`. Then combine it with `onPaginationChange` and `state.pagination` to control pagination and react to changes.
examples.heading: Pagination > Server side

examples.title: row-action-usage
examples.description:
Use the `DataTableAction` component to show links, buttons, or dropdown menus within rows that are only visible when the user hovers over the row.

You can enable the `primary` prop on any one of those actions to mark that as the primary action. This will automatically enable keyboard navigation within the table:

- Double click on row to perform primary action.
- Use up/down/left/right arrow keys to navigate between rows and actions.

Finally, make sure to use the `DataTableLabel` in your primary cell to set the label of the row for screen readers.

Hover over the rows to perform more actions:
examples.heading: Row actions

examples.title: row-selection-usage
examples.description:
Follow the row selection guide to allow selecting and highlighting rows.

Use the `DataTableCheckbox` component to automatically attach selection handlers and make the whole row selectable.

Combine `Checkbox`/`DataTableCheckbox` with `Cover` to make them easier to interact with by spanning the whole cell.

Finally, make sure to use the `DataTableLabel` in your primary cell to set the label of the row and the checkbox for screen readers.

Hover over the rows to see the checkboxes:
examples.heading: Row selection

examples.title: sorting-client-usage
examples.description:
Simply provide `getSortedRowModel` on table and optionally use `enableSorting` to control which columns you'd like to be sortable to use client-side sorting.

Hover over and click the table headers to sort by columns:
examples.heading: Sorting > Client side

examples.title: sorting-server-usage
examples.description:
To implement manual server-side sorting we can use `manualSorting`. Then combine it with `onSortingChange` and `state.sorting` to control sorting and react to changes.

Hover over and click the table headers to sort by columns:
examples.heading: Sorting > Server side

examples.title: sticky-column-usage
examples.description: Follow the column pinning guide and use the `columnPinning` option to pin columns either to the left or right side of the table.
examples.heading: Column pinning

examples.title: sticky-header-usage
examples.description: Headers in `DataTable` are sticky by default. Set a height on the component to allow scrolling vertically when a large number of rows are present.
examples.heading: Vertical scrolling

examples.title: usage
examples.description: Use the `table` prop to pass a table instance returned from `useReactTable()` hook. At minimum make sure to include `columns`, `data`, and `getCoreRowModel` when using the hook.
examples.heading: Usage

examples.title: virtualized-usage
examples.description:
Table automatically uses virtualized rendering when rows and columns cross a certain threshold to improve rendering performance.

Columns will be virtualized when there are more than 20 columns in a table and rows will be virtualized when there are more than 20 rows rendered or if columns are also being virtualized.
examples.heading: Virtualized

DataTable.accessibility:
### Labels

- Put `DataTableLabel` in each row's primary cell. It names the row and its selection checkbox for screen readers.

### Keyboard navigation

- Mark one `DataTableAction` per row as `primary` to enable arrow key navigation between rows and actions.

DataTableAction.description: DataTableAction component from Axiom Design System
DataTableAction.name: DataTableAction

DateInput.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space` | When focus is on `DateInput`, opens the calendar and focuses the selected day (or today's date). When focus is on a day, selects the focused day. |
| `Enter` | Selects the focused day in the calendar. |
| `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight`, `ArrowLeft` | Navigate between days in the calendar. |
| `PageUp`, `PageDown` | Navigate between months in the calendar. |
| `Shift+PageUp`, `Shift+PageDown` | Navigate between years in the calendar. |
| `Esc` | Closes the calendar popover and moves focus back to `DateInput`. |

Dialog.description:
Display a modal dialog box.

DialogHeader automatically includes a close button (X) in the top-right
corner - do not manually add a close button to the header.

Use Dialog for forms, data entry, content display, multi-step workflows, and
non-critical interactions. For confirmations or destructive actions, use
AlertDialog instead (which has no close button and requires explicit user
choice).

For forms, wrap DialogBody and DialogFooter in DialogForm and use
type="submit" on the primary action button.

A modal Dialog blocks pointer and focus outside itself, so overlays from
other libraries or scripts (react-select menus, MUI dialogs, Google's file
picker) need setup to stay usable. Keep the Dialog modal and follow the
{@link https://optimizely-axiom.github.io/optiaxiom/guides/nested-overlays/ Nested Overlays guide}.

code.content:
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogBody,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger>Open Dialog</DialogTrigger>

      <DialogContent size="sm">
        <DialogHeader>Modal Title</DialogHeader>

        <DialogBody>This is the modal body</DialogBody>

        <DialogFooter>
          <Dialog>
            <DialogTrigger mr="auto">Open nested dialog</DialogTrigger>

            <DialogContent size="sm">
              <DialogHeader>Modal Title</DialogHeader>

              <DialogBody>This is the modal body</DialogBody>

              <DialogFooter>
                <Dialog>
                  <DialogTrigger mr="auto">Open nested dialog</DialogTrigger>

                  <DialogContent size="sm">
                    <DialogHeader>Modal Title</DialogHeader>

                    <DialogBody>This is the modal body</DialogBody>

                    <DialogFooter>
                      <DialogClose appearance="primary">Close</DialogClose>
                    </DialogFooter>
                  </DialogContent>
                </Dialog>
                <DialogClose appearance="primary">Close</DialogClose>
              </DialogFooter>
            </DialogContent>
          </Dialog>
          <DialogClose appearance="primary">Close</DialogClose>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}

Dialog.accessibility:
### Labels

- Render a `DialogHeader`: its children become the dialog's accessible name. Use its `description` prop to add an accessible description.

### Focus

Focus moves into the dialog when it opens, stays inside while it's open, and returns to the trigger, or the element focused before it opened, when it closes.

### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space`, `Enter` | When focus is on `DialogTrigger`, opens the dialog. |
| `Esc` | Closes the dialog and moves focus to `DialogTrigger`. |

Control the size/width of the dialog box.

Size guidelines:
- sm (400px): Simple forms, confirmations, 1-2 input fields
- md (600-800px, default): Standard forms, 3-5 fields, medium content
- lg (900-1400px): Complex forms, wide tables, multi-column layouts
- fullscreen: Very large content, editors, dashboards

💡 Tip: When matching designs from screenshots, compare the content
density and layout complexity against these guidelines. Start with 'md'
(default) and only increase if the design clearly shows wider content or
multi-column layouts.

"use client";

import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLabel,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger>Profile</DropdownMenuTrigger>

      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuLabel>My Profile</DropdownMenuLabel>
        <DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>Settings</DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuSubContent>
            <DropdownMenuItem>Privacy</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem>Security</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem>Policy</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuSubContent>
        </DropdownMenuSub>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem>Logout</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}

Field.description:
Wrapper for inputs to provide context such as label/help/required etc.

Size the `Field` (for example with `w`), not the input inside it. The input
stretches to the field's width, so the description, error and character
count line up with it.

When the input sets `maxLength`, add `showCount` so users see how close they
are to the limit. Typing otherwise stops at the limit with no feedback.

Field.accessibility:
### Labels and errors

Field automatically handles accessibility attributes for you:

- Associates labels with inputs using `htmlFor` and `id`
- Connects error and description text using `aria-describedby`
- Generates unique IDs for labels and inputs

You can override the auto-generated IDs using the `inputId` and `labelId` props if needed for custom integrations.

- Icon + text combos: <Group gap="4" alignItems="center"><Icon /><Text /></Group>

Heading.description:
Renders semantic heading elements (h1-h4) for document structure and
accessibility.

Use this for page titles, section headings, and any text that represents a
heading in the document outline. Don't use Text with large fontSize and bold
fontWeight for headings - Heading provides proper semantics for screen
readers and improves accessibility.

When to use:
- Page titles
- Section headings
- Card/panel titles
- Any text with fontSize='xl'+ and fontWeight='500'+

⚠️ All heading levels (1-4) default to fontWeight="700". If your design shows
lighter headings, explicitly set fontWeight="500" or "600".

Set the font size with `fontSize`. `size` sets width and height, not font
size.

Don't use Text component for headings - it lacks semantic meaning.
Heading.name: Heading

code.content:
import { Field, Group, Input } from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Group flexDirection="column" gap="16">
      <Field label="Price">
        <Input addonBefore="$" placeholder="0.00" type="number" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Discount">
        <Input addonAfter="%" placeholder="0" type="number" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Weight">
        <Input addonAfter="kg" placeholder="0" type="number" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Website">
        <Input addonBefore="https://" placeholder="example.com" type="url" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Username">
        <Input addonBefore="@" placeholder="username" />
      </Field>
    </Group>
  );
}

Note: This only provides visual feedback. For actual validation, use the native `required` attribute on the Input or a form validation library like react-hook-form.
examples.heading: Required

examples.title: size-usage
examples.description: Use the `size` prop to control the size of the input field. The `xl` size uses a larger font size for the input value and placeholder.
examples.heading: Sizes

code.content:
import { Field, Group, Input } from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Group flexDirection="column" gap="16">
      <Field label="Email">
        <Input placeholder="name@example.com" type="email" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Password">
        <Input placeholder="Enter password" type="password" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Phone number">
        <Input placeholder="+1 (555) 000-0000" type="tel" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Website">
        <Input placeholder="https://example.com" type="url" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Number">
        <Input placeholder="0" type="number" />
      </Field>
    </Group>
  );
}

examples.title: type-usage
examples.description: Use the `type` prop to specify the type of data the input should accept. Common types include `email`, `password`, `tel`, `url`, and `number`.
examples.heading: Input types

Input.accessibility:
### Labels and errors

Wrap Input in `Field` to connect it to its label, description and error message:

- The label's `for` points at the input's `id`.
- `aria-describedby` references the description and error message.
- `aria-invalid` is set when the field has an error.

### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to or away from the input |
| `Shift + Tab` | Moves focus to the previous focusable element |

LabelMenuButton.description:
Button displaying both a label and value, used as the trigger for Select or
Menu. Use it with Select when the choice is a form value. Use it with Menu
(via `MenuTrigger asChild`) when picking applies immediately as view state,
such as a filter on a list page, with `selected` options and `execute`
handlers.

Menu.description:
Dropdown menu for actions, multi-select, and complex interactions.
Supports a search input that filters options as the user types
(autocomplete), options that create a new item from the typed text,
checkbox/radio items, nested sub-menus, links, and action handlers via
`execute`.

Must be used with MenuTrigger and MenuContent sub-components. MenuTrigger
automatically renders a button with chevron icon, or use MenuTrigger asChild
with custom buttons like EllipsisMenuButton for overflow menus.

Use Menu when: action menus (edit/delete/archive), multi-select dropdowns,
filterable lists, nested menus, items with links/navigation, or view filters
that apply immediately (e.g. on a list page).

Use Select instead when: you need a simple single-select form input
with `value`/`onChange` and form submission support.

Note: Menu is not a form control - it has no `value`/`onChange` and does
not integrate with `Field`. For a single-select form field, use Select
(which does not support filtering). There is currently no built-in
combobox (a filterable single-select form input).
Menu.name: Menu

intent.description: Control the appearance by selecting between the different item types.

examples.title: addon-usage
examples.description: We can add the `addon` property to show additional content inside the items.
examples.heading: Addon

examples.title: alert-dialog-usage
examples.description:
Combine with dialogs to show modals or alerts when selecting an item.

Make sure to use `AlertDialog` or `Dialog` in controlled mode since there is no actual trigger.
examples.heading: Dialogs inside menus

examples.title: appearance-usage
examples.description: Use the `intent` prop to control the appearance of items.
examples.heading: Appearance

examples.title: basic-usage
examples.description:
Menu works with lists of items provided via the `options` prop. The basic structure includes the main component provider, a trigger, and the content popover.

- `Menu`
- `MenuTrigger`
- `MenuContent`

Items must be an array of objects of `MenuOption` type.

examples.title: content-checkbox-usage
examples.description: We can render multi-select items by enabling the `multi` property.
examples.heading: Selection > Multi-select

examples.title: content-radio-switch-usage
examples.description: We can optionally use switch toggles to show selection states by enabling the `switch` property.
examples.heading: Selection > Single-select (Switch)

examples.title: content-radio-usage
examples.description: Now that we can perform actions on selection, we can also store that state and show the selected states for each item using the `selected` property.
examples.heading: Selection > Single-select

examples.title: content-usage
examples.description: Clicking the items will not do anything yet. For that we'll have to add the `execute` property to each item.
examples.heading: Selection

examples.title: creatable-usage
examples.description:
We can customize the filter behavior using the `visible` property on items.

The following example shows how we can build **creatable** menus by allowing the user to add new entries on the fly.
examples.heading: Input > Creatable example

examples.title: description-usage
examples.description: We can use the `description` property to show secondary text in addition to item labels.
examples.heading: Description

examples.title: detail-usage
examples.description: We can use the `detail` property to show secondary content in addition to item labels.
examples.heading: Detail

examples.title: disabled-usage
examples.description: Use the `disabledReason` property to disable the menu items.
examples.heading: Disabled items

examples.title: ellipsis-trigger-usage
examples.description:
We can also use `asChild` to render a completely different component. We provide two built-in buttons:

- `AngleMenuButton` (default)
- `EllipsisMenuButton`
examples.heading: Trigger > Ellipsis trigger

examples.title: empty-usage
examples.description: By default menu will display a generic empty content message if no results are found matching your query. We can customize this empty message by setting the `empty` prop.
examples.heading: Empty

examples.title: group-hidden-usage
examples.description: Use `group.hidden` property to hide the group label. Useful when you want to separate groups but do not want show any labels.
examples.heading: Groups > Hidden label

examples.title: group-priority-usage
examples.description: Use `group.priority` property to sort groups among each other.
examples.heading: Groups > Priority

examples.title: group-separator-usage
examples.description: Use `group.separator` to show a horizontal separator before/after the group.
examples.heading: Groups > Separator

examples.title: group-usage
examples.description: Use `group` property to group items.
examples.heading: Groups

examples.title: input-controlled-usage
examples.description:
We can also manually control `options` in combination with the `inputValue` and `onInputValueChange` prop to load items as the user types.

And we can toggle the `loading` prop to show a loading state while the data is loading (an empty state will be shown otherwise).
examples.heading: Input > Async loading example

examples.title: input-usage
examples.description: By default the input is only shown if there are any selectable items (items with a `selected` property) or when the user starts typing. But we can always show the input by setting the `inputVisible` prop to `always`.
examples.heading: Input

examples.title: keyword-usage
examples.description:
Menu automatically handles filtering using a built-in fuzzy filter based on the `label` and `keywords` properties of items.

Type "placeholder" into the menu and see how "Workflow" is highlighted:
examples.heading: Input > Filtering

examples.title: link-execute-usage
examples.description:
Add the `href` property to options to render them as links.

If the `execute` property is also present then the default link clicking behavior will be prevented (unless users use a modifier like Enter to open in a new tab).
examples.heading: Links

examples.title: link-external-usage
examples.description: We can toggle the `external` property to show an external link icon and open links in a new tab by default.
examples.heading: Links > External

examples.title: link-usage
examples.description: If the `execute` property is omitted then clicking an item will simply follow the link and close the menu.
examples.heading: Links

examples.title: nested-usage
examples.description: Use `subOptions` property to render submenus.
examples.heading: Submenus

examples.title: trigger-usage
examples.description: By default we use the `Button` component for the menu trigger which accepts all of the existing button props.
examples.heading: Trigger > Customize trigger

examples.title: virtualized-usage
examples.description: Menu automatically uses virtualization to improve performance when rendering a large number of items.
examples.heading: Virtualized

Menu.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space` | When focus is on `MenuTrigger`, opens the menu and focuses the first item (or selected item). When focus is on an item, activates the focused item. |
| `Enter` | When focus is on `MenuTrigger`, opens the menu and focuses the first item (or selected item). When focus is on an item, activates the focused item and closes the menu. |
| `ArrowDown` | When focus is on `MenuTrigger`, opens the menu and focuses the first item (or selected item). When focus is on an item, moves focus to the next item. |
| `ArrowUp` | When focus is on an item, moves focus to the previous item. |
| `PageUp`, `PageDown` | Moves focus up/down by 10 items at a time. |
| `Home`, `End` | Moves focus to the first/last item. |
| `ArrowRight`, `ArrowLeft` | When focus is on an item with a submenu, opens/closes the submenu. |
| `A - Z` | When focus is on an item, filter and display matching items as you type. |
| `Esc` | Closes the menu and moves focus back to `MenuTrigger`. |

examples.title: usage
examples.description:
Dialog and popover components internally use focus managers to ensure focus trapping works consistently across browsers. This works for all elements inside the DOM tree of the dialog/popover, but elements rendered via portals are not automatically tracked.

All of our components automatically handle this focus management when being rendered inside dialogs/popovers - but third party portalled components need to be manually wrapped in the `ModalLayer` component.

Change the default rendered element for the one passed as a child, merging their props and behavior.

Read the {@link https://optimizely-axiom.github.io/optiaxiom/components/#composition Composition guide} for more details.

bg.description: Set the element's background color. Only accepts predefined color tokens starting with `bg.` (e.g., `bg.default`, `bg.accent`, `bg.error`), or the special values `current` and `transparent`.

borderColor.description: Set the element's border color. Only accepts predefined color tokens starting with `border.` (e.g., `border.default`, `border.accent`, `border.error`), or the special values `current` and `transparent`.

color.description: Set the element's text color. Only accepts predefined color tokens starting with `fg.` (e.g., `fg.default`, `fg.accent`, `fg.error`), or the special values `current` and `transparent`.

flex.description:
Set the element's `flex` CSS property. `1` grows to fill available
space; `auto` grows and shrinks to fit content; `initial` shrinks but
does not grow; `none` neither grows nor shrinks (use this instead of
`flex-shrink: 0`).

fontFamily.description: Set the element's font family. Only accepts predefined fontFamily tokens.

fontSize.description: Set the element's font size and line height (both properties are set together). Only accepts predefined fontSize tokens.

gridAutoRows.description:
Set the element's `grid-auto-rows` CSS property. The only value `fr`
sizes implicit rows to `minmax(0, 1fr)` (equal-height rows that can
shrink below their content).

gridColumn.description:
Set how many columns the element spans in a grid (`grid-column`). The
value is the span count, e.g. `2` spans 2 columns — NOT the column it
starts at.

gridTemplateColumns.description:
Control number of columns in a grid layout (`grid-template-columns`).
The value is the number of equal columns, e.g. `2` creates two equal
columns (`repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))`) — use this instead of a raw
`style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr" }}`.

h.description: Set the element's height. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

m.description: Set the element's margin on all sides. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

maxH.description: Set the element's maximum height. Only accepts predefined maxSize tokens.

maxW.description: Set the element's maximum width. Only accepts predefined maxSize tokens.

mb.description: Set the element's bottom margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

minH.description:
Set the element's minimum height. `0` lets a flex item shrink below its
content, e.g. so a flex column wrapping a scrolling list stays within its
parent and the list scrolls; `auto` restores the default.

minW.description:
Set the element's minimum width. `0` lets a flex item shrink below its
content, e.g. so a `Text` with `truncate` inside it can truncate; `auto`
restores the default.

ml.description: Set the element's left margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mr.description: Set the element's right margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mt.description: Set the element's top margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mx.description: Set the element's left and right margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

my.description: Set the element's top and bottom margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

onDismiss.description: Show a close button inside the pill and invoke this callback when the pill is clicked.

overflow.description:
Set the element's `overflow` CSS property

Inside nested flex columns, every flex item between the scroll container
and the fixed-height ancestor also needs `minH="0"`, or it grows to fit
the content and nothing scrolls.

p.description: Set the element's padding on all sides. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pb.description: Set the element's bottom padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pl.description: Set the element's left padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pr.description: Set the element's right padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pt.description: Set the element's top padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

px.description: Set the element's left and right padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

py.description: Set the element's top and bottom padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

readOnly.description:
When true, the pill is rendered as a non-interactive span element instead
of a button. Use this for display-only pills that don't respond to
clicks.

rounded.description: Set the element's border radius. Only accepts predefined borderRadius tokens.

shadow.description: Set the element's box shadow. Only accepts predefined boxShadow tokens.

size.description: Control the size of the pill.

transition.description:
Control which CSS properties should transition. Each value is a preset:
`colors` transitions color-related properties (background, border,
color, fill, stroke, text-decoration); `opacity` and `transform`
transition just that property; `all` transitions everything; `none`
disables transitions.

w.description: Set the element's width. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

z.description: Set the element's stacking order. Only accepts predefined zIndex tokens (e.g., popover, toast, tooltip) or numeric values (0, 10, 20, 30, auto).

examples.title: disabled-usage
examples.description:
Set the `disabled` prop to `true` to disable pills and prevent any interactions.

Include visible text that explains why it's disabled: a disabled pill leaves the tab order, so keyboard and screen reader users can't reach a tooltip on it.
examples.heading: Disabled state

examples.title: dismiss-usage
examples.description: Use the `onDismiss` prop to show a close button inside the pill.
examples.heading: Dismissible

examples.title: group-usage
examples.description: Use the `<PillGroup />` component to group related pills together.
examples.heading: Grouping pills

examples.title: size-usage
examples.description: Use the `size` prop to modify the size of the button.
examples.heading: Different sizes

Pill.accessibility:
### Labels

- A disabled pill leaves the tab order. Explain why it's disabled in visible text nearby.

code.content:
import { IconGrid, IconRectangleList, IconSliders } from "@optiaxiom/icons";
import {
  Field,
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverTrigger,
  SegmentedControl,
  SegmentedControlItem,
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectTrigger,
  Separator,
  Tooltip,
} from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger icon={<IconSliders />}>Display</PopoverTrigger>

      <PopoverContent align="end" gap="12" px="0">
        <SegmentedControl defaultValue="list" gap="12" px="16">
          <Tooltip content="List">
            <SegmentedControlItem
              aria-label="List"
              icon={<IconRectangleList />}
              size="lg"
              value="list"
            />
          </Tooltip>

          <Tooltip content="Grid">
            <SegmentedControlItem
              aria-label="Grid"
              icon={<IconGrid />}
              size="lg"
              value="grid"
            />
          </Tooltip>
        </SegmentedControl>

        <Field
          flexDirection="row"
          justifyContent="space-between"
          label="Columns"
          px="16"
        >
          <Select
            defaultValue="Status"
            options={[
              { label: "Status", value: "Status" },
              { label: "Due Dates", value: "Due Dates" },
            ]}
          >
            <SelectTrigger ml="12" size="sm" />
            <SelectContent align="end" />
          </Select>
        </Field>

        <Field
          flexDirection="row"
          justifyContent="space-between"
          label="Grouping"
          px="16"
        >
          <Select
            defaultValue="No grouping"
            options={[
              { label: "No grouping", value: "No grouping" },
              { label: "Campaign", value: "Campaign" },
            ]}
          >
            <SelectTrigger ml="12" size="sm" />
            <SelectContent align="end" />
          </Select>
        </Field>

        <Separator orientation="horizontal" />

        <Field
          flexDirection="row"
          justifyContent="space-between"
          label="View"
          px="16"
        >
          <Select
            defaultValue="Tasks"
            options={[
              { label: "Tasks", value: "Tasks" },
              { label: "Steps", value: "Steps" },
            ]}
          >
            <SelectTrigger ml="12" size="sm" />
            <SelectContent align="end" />
          </Select>
        </Field>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}

RadioGroup.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus into and out of the radio group |
| `Space` | Selects the focused radio if not already selected |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight` | Moves focus to and selects the next radio |
| `ArrowUp`, `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus to and selects the previous radio |

RadioGroup automatically handles accessibility:

- Uses proper `role="radiogroup"` and individual `role="radio"` attributes
- Supports `aria-checked` for selected state
- Groups radios with proper keyboard navigation

### Labels

- Wrap Range in `Field` for a visible label, or pass `aria-label` when there isn't one.

### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ArrowUp`, `ArrowLeft` | Increments by the `step` value. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight` | Decrements by the `step` value. |
| `PageUp`, `PageDown` | Increments/decrements by a larger step value. |
| `Home` | Sets the value to its minimum. |
| `End` | Sets the value to its maximum. |

bg.description: Set the element's background color. Only accepts predefined color tokens starting with `bg.` (e.g., `bg.default`, `bg.accent`, `bg.error`), or the special values `current` and `transparent`.

borderColor.description: Set the element's border color. Only accepts predefined color tokens starting with `border.` (e.g., `border.default`, `border.accent`, `border.error`), or the special values `current` and `transparent`.

defaultValue.description:
The value of the item that is pressed when initially rendered. Use
`defaultValue` if you do not need to control the state of a toggle group.
The value of the items that are pressed when initially rendered. Use

disabled.description:
Whether the group is disabled from user interaction.
@defaultValue false

flex.description:
Set the element's `flex` CSS property. `1` grows to fill available
space; `auto` grows and shrinks to fit content; `initial` shrinks but
does not grow; `none` neither grows nor shrinks (use this instead of
`flex-shrink: 0`).

fontFamily.description: Set the element's font family. Only accepts predefined fontFamily tokens.

fontSize.description: Set the element's font size and line height (both properties are set together). Only accepts predefined fontSize tokens.

gridAutoRows.description:
Set the element's `grid-auto-rows` CSS property. The only value `fr`
sizes implicit rows to `minmax(0, 1fr)` (equal-height rows that can
shrink below their content).

gridColumn.description:
Set how many columns the element spans in a grid (`grid-column`). The
value is the span count, e.g. `2` spans 2 columns — NOT the column it
starts at.

gridTemplateColumns.description:
Control number of columns in a grid layout (`grid-template-columns`).
The value is the number of equal columns, e.g. `2` creates two equal
columns (`repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))`) — use this instead of a raw
`style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr" }}`.

h.description: Set the element's height. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

m.description: Set the element's margin on all sides. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

maxH.description: Set the element's maximum height. Only accepts predefined maxSize tokens.

maxW.description: Set the element's maximum width. Only accepts predefined maxSize tokens.

mb.description: Set the element's bottom margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

minH.description:
Set the element's minimum height. `0` lets a flex item shrink below its
content, e.g. so a flex column wrapping a scrolling list stays within its
parent and the list scrolls; `auto` restores the default.

minW.description:
Set the element's minimum width. `0` lets a flex item shrink below its
content, e.g. so a `Text` with `truncate` inside it can truncate; `auto`
restores the default.

ml.description: Set the element's left margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mr.description: Set the element's right margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mt.description: Set the element's top margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mx.description: Set the element's left and right margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

my.description: Set the element's top and bottom margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

onValueChange.description:
The callback that fires when the value of the toggle group changes.
The callback that fires when the state of the toggle group changes.

overflow.description:
Set the element's `overflow` CSS property

Inside nested flex columns, every flex item between the scroll container
and the fixed-height ancestor also needs `minH="0"`, or it grows to fit
the content and nothing scrolls.

py.description: Set the element's top and bottom padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

rounded.description: Set the element's border radius. Only accepts predefined borderRadius tokens.

rovingFocus.description:
Whether the group should maintain roving focus of its buttons.
@defaultValue true

shadow.description: Set the element's box shadow. Only accepts predefined boxShadow tokens.

size.description:
Set the element's width and height. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

When width and height are the same, use `size` instead of setting both
`w` and `h` separately (e.g., prefer `size="24"` over `w="24" h="24"`).

transition.description:
Control which CSS properties should transition. Each value is a preset:
`colors` transitions color-related properties (background, border,
color, fill, stroke, text-decoration); `opacity` and `transform`
transition just that property; `all` transitions everything; `none`
disables transitions.

type.description: Whether to allow multiple values or only activate one item at a time.

value.description:
The controlled stateful value of the item that is pressed.
The controlled stateful value of the items that are pressed.

w.description: Set the element's width. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

z.description: Set the element's stacking order. Only accepts predefined zIndex tokens (e.g., popover, toast, tooltip) or numeric values (0, 10, 20, 30, auto).

SegmentedControl.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to either the pressed item or the first item in the group. |
| `Space`, `Enter` | Activates/deactivates the item. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight` | Moves focus to the next item in the group. |
| `ArrowUp`, `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus to the previous item in the group. |
| `Home`, `End` | Moves focus to the first/last item. |

Select.description:
Single-select form input for choosing one value from a dropdown list.
Works like a native `<select>` — supports `name`, `value`, `onChange`,
and works with `<form>` submissions.

Must be used with SelectTrigger and SelectContent sub-components.

Use Select when: single value selection in a form, controlled/uncontrolled
form input, you need form submission support.

Use Menu instead when: you need multi-select, actions (edit/delete),
links, filtering/search, nested sub-menus, or checkbox/radio items.
Select.name: Select

defaultValue.description: The initial selected value in uncontrolled mode.

onChange.description: Native `change` event handler for the hidden select element. Prefer `onValueChange` for most use cases.

detail.description: Secondary text displayed next to the label.

disabledReason.description:
Mark the item as disabled and show the reason in a tooltip. The item can
still be reached by keyboard, but not selected.

group.description: Provide an optional group that item belongs to.

hidden.description: Whether the group label should be hidden or not.

label.description: The label group.

priority.description:
The sorting priority of the group (default: 0).
Groups with higher priority are sorted first.

separator.description: Whether to display a separator before this group.

group.title: SelectOptionGroup

label.description: String representation of items.

value.description:
The value submitted with the form and passed to `onValueChange`. Must be
unique.

Use `""` for a "none" option: selecting it clears the value, so the
trigger shows its `placeholder` and `required` treats the field as empty.
Give the option a non-empty value (e.g. `"all"`) when its label should
show in the trigger, such as an "All" filter.

required.description: Whether the select value is required.

value.description: The selected value in controlled mode.

examples.description:
By default we use the `Button` component for the menu trigger which accepts all of the existing button props.

We can also use `asChild` to render a completely different component. We provide a few built-in buttons:

- [`AngleMenuButton`](/components/angle-menu-button/) (default)
- [`LabelMenuButton`](/components/label-menu-button/)
examples.heading: Trigger

examples.title: usage
examples.description:
Select works with lists of items provided via the `options` prop. The basic structure includes the main component provider, a trigger, and the content.

- `Select`
- `SelectTrigger`
- `SelectContent`

Items must be an array of objects of `SelectOption` type and at minimum must contain the following two properties:

- `label`
- `value`

The trigger can be provided a `placeholder` to display in case no values have been selected yet (or if an empty value is selected).
examples.heading: Structure

Select.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space`, `Enter` | When focus is on `SelectTrigger`, opens the menu and focuses the first item (or selected item). When focus is on an item, activates the focused item and closes the menu. |
| `ArrowDown` | When focus is on `SelectTrigger`, opens the menu and focuses the first item (or selected item). When focus is on an item, moves focus to the next item. |
| `ArrowUp` | When focus is on `SelectTrigger`, opens the menu and focuses the last item (or selected item). When focus is on an item, moves focus to the previous item. |
| `PageUp`, `PageDown` | Moves focus up/down by 10 items at a time. |
| `Home`, `End` | Moves focus to the first/last item. |
| `Esc` | Closes the menu and moves focus back to `SelectTrigger`. |

examples.title: basic-usage
examples.description:
`Sortable` works with a list of items provided via the `items` prop. Each item is a unique string identifying the sortable item within the list, or an object with a unique `id` and a `label` (see Screen reader announcements).

Next we provide a render prop in `children` that has the same `items` as an argument but representing the live state as they are being sorted.

Finally we use `SortableItem` to render each sortable element inside the render function.
examples.heading: Basic

examples.title: card-usage
examples.description: We can combine Sortable with the Card component to build a sortable list of cards.
examples.heading: Card example

examples.title: controlled-onchange-usage
examples.description: Using `onChange` is necessary in cases where we're sorting a large number of items and we only want to mutate the item that is being dragged.
examples.heading: Sorting

examples.title: controlled-usage
examples.description:
Notice in the previous demo items are draggable but they always revert back to their original position.

We need to use either the `onItemsChange` or `onChange` prop to store the new sorted state.

Only use either `onItemsChange` or `onChange`. Do not use both props on the same component.

Using `onValueChange` is the simplest way to handle sorting for smaller pieces of data where we can update the sorting rank for all items in one call.
examples.heading: Sorting

examples.title: handle-usage
examples.description: By default the whole item acts as the drag handle, but we can use the `SortableHandle` component to render separate drag handles within the items.
examples.heading: Drag handle

examples.title: label-usage
examples.description: While an item is dragged, screen readers announce its name and position, such as "Design moved to position 3 of 5". A string item is its own name. When IDs aren't readable, pass items as `{ id, label }` objects instead and the `label` is announced. A list must be all strings or all objects.
examples.heading: Screen reader announcements

examples.title: list-usage
examples.description:
Use the `SortableGroup` component to swap items between lists in addition to sorting with each other.

We also need to change the `items` prop to an object where the key is the ID of the group and the value is the list of items in that group.
examples.heading: Multiple lists

Sortable.accessibility:
### Announcements

- While an item is dragged, screen readers announce its name and new position. Pass items as `{ id, label }` objects when the IDs aren't readable.

separator.description: Whether to show separators around the whole group.

href.description: Render a link with the given value as the `href` attribute.

intent.description: Control the appearance by selecting between the different item types.

key.description: A unique key for the item, used to track its row. Defaults to the label, so pass a unique `key` whenever labels can repeat (e.g. options built from data).

keywords.description: Additional text to use for filtering items based on input value.

label.description: Return a string representation of item.

visible.description:

Switch.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Space` | Toggles the switch between on and off |
| `Enter` | Toggles the switch between on and off |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to or away from the switch |
| `Shift + Tab` | Moves focus to the previous focusable element |

Switch automatically handles accessibility:

- Uses proper `role="switch"` and ARIA attributes
- Supports `aria-checked` for on/off states
- Associates label text with the switch control

Table.description:
Display tabular data using rows and columns.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT**: Consider using `DataTable` instead for displaying tabular
data.

`DataTable` provides built-in support for:
- Sorting (client-side and server-side)
- Pagination (client-side and server-side)
- Row selection with checkboxes
- Column pinning (sticky columns)
- Row expansion
- Loading states
- Virtualization for large datasets

`Table` is a low-level primitive and should only be used for very specific
custom table layouts. For most use cases, `DataTable` is the recommended
choice.

Tabs.accessibility:
### Keyboard interactions

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | When focus moves onto the tabs, focuses the active trigger. When a trigger is focused, moves focus to the active content. |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight` | Moves focus to the next trigger depending on `orientation` and activates its associated content. |
| `ArrowUp`, `ArrowLeft` | Moves focus to the previous trigger depending on `orientation` and activates its associated content. |
| `Home`, `End` | Moves focus to the first/last trigger and activates its associated content. |

ToastProvider.description:
Provider component for toast notifications. This is included in AxiomProvider
by default - you only need to use this component directly for advanced
customization. Use `toaster.create()` to display toast messages.

A toast briefly confirms something that already happened, like "Changes
saved". It closes on its own, so nothing can depend on the user reading it or
clicking its action, and whatever the action does must be reachable
elsewhere too. Toasts with an action stay open 1.5× the provider's
`duration`. Don't use a toast for:

- Undo windows that hold a change back: apply the change right away and make
  the action restore it, without a confirmation dialog beforehand.
- Progress on running work: show it on the control that started it, with
  `Button` `loading` or an inline `Spinner`.
- Long or persistent messages: use `Banner` or `Alert`.
ToastProvider.name: ToastProvider

ToastProvider.accessibility:
### Announcements

- Toasts are announced to screen readers when they appear. Keep the message short and self-contained.
- Keyboard users press `F8` to move focus to the toasts. The timer pauses while focus or the pointer is on a toast.
- A toast closes on its own, so keep whatever its action does reachable elsewhere too.

ToggleButton.accessibility:
### Labels

- Give an icon only toggle button an `aria-label`. ToggleButton exposes its state with `aria-pressed`, so keep the label the same in both states.
- A disabled toggle button leaves the tab order. Explain why it's disabled in visible text nearby.

Tooltip.description:
Popup with brief information shown when user interacts with an element using
keyboard focus or mouse hover.

Keep content to a short plain-text label of a few words. For longer, rich or
interactive help use Popover opened from a labelled button instead: a
tooltip closes when the pointer moves onto it and doesn't open on tap.

The child must be focusable or contain a focusable element, otherwise
keyboard users can't open the tooltip.

Set the element's `flex` CSS property. `1` grows to fill available
space; `auto` grows and shrinks to fit content; `initial` shrinks but
does not grow; `none` neither grows nor shrinks (use this instead of
`flex-shrink: 0`).

fontFamily.description: Set the element's font family. Only accepts predefined fontFamily tokens.

fontSize.description: Set the element's font size and line height (both properties are set together). Only accepts predefined fontSize tokens.

gridAutoRows.description:
Set the element's `grid-auto-rows` CSS property. The only value `fr`
sizes implicit rows to `minmax(0, 1fr)` (equal-height rows that can
shrink below their content).

gridColumn.description:
Set how many columns the element spans in a grid (`grid-column`). The
value is the span count, e.g. `2` spans 2 columns — NOT the column it
starts at.

gridTemplateColumns.description:
Control number of columns in a grid layout (`grid-template-columns`).
The value is the number of equal columns, e.g. `2` creates two equal
columns (`repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))`) — use this instead of a raw
`style={{ gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr" }}`.

h.description: Set the element's height. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

m.description: Set the element's margin on all sides. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

maxH.description: Set the element's maximum height. Only accepts predefined maxSize tokens.

maxW.description: Set the element's maximum width. Only accepts predefined maxSize tokens.

mb.description: Set the element's bottom margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

minH.description:
Set the element's minimum height. `0` lets a flex item shrink below its
content, e.g. so a flex column wrapping a scrolling list stays within its
parent and the list scrolls; `auto` restores the default.

minW.description:
Set the element's minimum width. `0` lets a flex item shrink below its
content, e.g. so a `Text` with `truncate` inside it can truncate; `auto`
restores the default.

ml.description: Set the element's left margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mr.description: Set the element's right margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mt.description: Set the element's top margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

mx.description: Set the element's left and right margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

my.description: Set the element's top and bottom margin. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

onEscapeKeyDown.description:
Event handler called when the escape key is down.
Can be prevented.

onOpenChange.description: Handler that is called when the open state changes.

onPointerDownOutside.description:
Event handler called when the a `pointerdown` event happens outside of the `Tooltip`.
Can be prevented.

open.description: The open state in controlled mode.

overflow.description:
Set the element's `overflow` CSS property

Inside nested flex columns, every flex item between the scroll container
and the fixed-height ancestor also needs `minH="0"`, or it grows to fit
the content and nothing scrolls.

p.description: Set the element's padding on all sides. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pb.description: Set the element's bottom padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pl.description: Set the element's left padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pr.description: Set the element's right padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

pt.description: Set the element's top padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

px.description: Set the element's left and right padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

py.description: Set the element's top and bottom padding. Only accepts predefined spacing tokens.

rounded.description: Set the element's border radius. Only accepts predefined borderRadius tokens.

shadow.description: Set the element's box shadow. Only accepts predefined boxShadow tokens.

size.description:
Set the element's width and height. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

When width and height are the same, use `size` instead of setting both
`w` and `h` separately (e.g., prefer `size="24"` over `w="24" h="24"`).

transition.description:
Control which CSS properties should transition. Each value is a preset:
`colors` transitions color-related properties (background, border,
color, fill, stroke, text-decoration); `opacity` and `transform`
transition just that property; `all` transitions everything; `none`
disables transitions.

w.description: Set the element's width. Only accepts predefined size tokens.

z.description: Set the element's stacking order. Only accepts predefined zIndex tokens (e.g., popover, toast, tooltip) or numeric values (0, 10, 20, 30, auto).

Tooltip.accessibility:
### Trigger and content

- The trigger must be focusable or contain a focusable element, since keyboard users open the tooltip by focusing it.
- Keep content to a short plain-text label. A tooltip doesn't open on tap and closes when the pointer moves onto it, so put longer or interactive help in a [Popover](https://optimizely-axiom.github.io/optiaxiom/components/popover/).

TooltipProvider.description: Provider component for tooltips. This is included in AxiomProvider by default - you only need to use this component directly for advanced customization.
TooltipProvider.name: TooltipProvider

delayDuration.description:
The duration from when the pointer enters the trigger until the tooltip gets opened.
@defaultValue 700

disableHoverableContent.description: When `true`, trying to hover the content will result in the tooltip closing as the pointer leaves the trigger.

skipDelayDuration.description:
How much time a user has to enter another trigger without incurring a delay again.
@defaultValue 300

Transition.description: Component for animating element transitions with fade and pop effects.
Transition.name: Transition

duration.description: Control the duration of the animation.

skipAnimations.description: Whether to skip the animation or not. Useful for initial mount and unit testing.

type.description:
The properties to animate during transition.
 - fade: only animate the opacity
 - pop: animate the opacity, scale, and translate (depending on data-side)

examples.title: colors-usage
examples.description: Use `transition="colors"` to transition all color related properties.
examples.heading: Transition colors

getting-started.content:
# Getting Started

> **Note:** 
  Want to skip the docs? Try our [MCP Server](/guides/mcp/)

## Installation

### Install package

Install the `@optiaxiom/react` package using your package manager of choice:

```sh npm2yarn
npm install @optiaxiom/react
```

### Setup CSS imports

Make sure to configure your bundler to handle [CSS Imports](/guides/css-imports).

### Add global provider

Wrap your application with [AxiomProvider](/components/axiom-provider):

```jsx
import { AxiomProvider } from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return <AxiomProvider>{/* Your app code here */}</AxiomProvider>;
}
```

## Usage

### Basic usage

Import components from `@optiaxiom/react` and use them:

```jsx
import { Button } from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function MyComponent() {
  return <Button>Hello World!</Button>;
}
```

### What to read next

fonts.content:
# Fonts (Optimizely staff only)

We ship our licensed brand fonts as a private package for use with our Optimizely Design System.

> **Note:** 
**Optimizely staff** should always use the fonts from our **`@optimizely/axiom-fonts`** package.

**Third party developers** can skip this package - we automatically fall back to free web fonts.

## Installation

### Install package

Make sure you have access to our private package repository and install the `@optimizely/axiom-fonts` package.

```sh npm2yarn
npm install @optimizely/axiom-fonts
```

### Basic usage

Add a bare import statement at the top of your application's entry point (such as your root layout or main entry file) so the fonts CSS gets loaded.

```tsx
import "@optimizely/axiom-fonts";
```

Make sure the import stays static and synchronous - keep it as a top-level `import` rather than a dynamic `import()` or lazy-loaded module - so the fonts are available from first paint and you avoid a flash of fallback fonts.

## How it works

### Font fallbacks

Our font stacks already list our **licensed brand fonts** first, followed by free web fonts. The free fonts are loaded automatically by the design system, so text always renders.

### Loading the brand fonts

The `@optimizely/axiom-fonts` package adds the `@font-face` declarations for the brand fonts. Once it's imported, the browser uses them at the front of the stack; without it, text gracefully falls back to the free web fonts.

typography.content:
# Typography

Text in Axiom comes from two places: the `Heading` and `Text` components, which say what a
piece of text **is**, and the font style props, which set individual **values**. Reach for a
component first.

## Documentation

### Headings

Use `Heading` for page titles, section headings, and card or panel titles. The `level` prop
controls the semantic tag, font size, and line height together, so the page keeps a correct
document outline for screen readers. Levels run from `1` to `4`.

```tsx
import { Group, Heading } from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Group flexDirection="column" gap="16">
      <Heading level="1">This is h1 heading</Heading>
      <Heading level="2">This is h2 heading</Heading>
      <Heading level="3">This is h3 heading</Heading>
      <Heading level="4">This is h4 heading</Heading>
    </Group>
  );
}
```

Because the sizes come from the design library, don't override `fontSize` on a `Heading` —
pick the `level` that matches. Two adjustments are expected:

- Every level defaults to `fontWeight="700"`. If the design shows a lighter heading, set
  `fontWeight="500"` or `"600"` explicitly.
- To use one level's visual size under a different tag, combine `level` with `asChild` — see
  [Heading](/components/heading/).

### Body text

Use `Text` for paragraphs, captions, descriptions, and any other non-heading copy. It
renders a ``, which cannot be nested inside another `` — for inline styling within a
paragraph, use `asChild` with a `<span>`.

```tsx
import { Group, Text } from "@optiaxiom/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <Group flexDirection="column" gap="16">
      <Text fontSize="xs">Extra small text</Text>
      <Text fontSize="sm">Small text</Text>
      <Text fontSize="md">Default text</Text>
      <Text fontSize="lg">Large text</Text>
      <Text fontSize="xl">Extra large text</Text>
    </Group>
  );
}
```

Body copy is where the font props belong: [fontSize](/props/font-size/),
[fontWeight](/props/font-weight/), [fontFamily](/props/font-family/) and
[color](/props/color/), which takes `fg.` tokens. Each page lists the values
available.

### When it is really a heading

If text ends up at `fontSize="xl"` or larger **and** `fontWeight="500"` or heavier, it is a
heading — reach for the component instead. Styling `Text` to look like one produces the
right pixels with none of the semantics:

```jsx
// Don't do this
<Text fontSize="2xl" fontWeight="700">
  Section title
</Text>

// Do this
<Heading level="2">Section title</Heading>
```

If you are coming from Figma, `Heading` and `Text` are the text styles. The font props are
the equivalent of overriding size or weight on a single layer.

group-migration.content:
# Flex to Group migration ## Why Group? ### Background The [Flex](/components/flex) component has non-standard defaults that cause confusion for developers and AI tools. [Group](/components/group) is the replacement with CSS-standard defaults that align with how flexbox works in standard CSS. ### Key differences | Property | Flex (deprecated) | Group (new) | | ------------- | ----------------- | -------------------- | | flexDirection | "column" | "row" (CSS standard) | | gap | "16" | no default | ## Migration examples ### Vertical grouping (most common old usage) ```tsx // Before
1
2
 // After
1
2
 ``` ### Horizontal layout ```tsx // Before
1
2
 // After
1
2
 ``` Note: Since Group defaults to `flexDirection="row"`, you don't need to specify it explicitly. ### With custom gap ```tsx // Before
1
2
 // After
1
2
 ``` ### Horizontal with custom gap ```tsx // Before
1
2
 // After
1
2
 ``` ### Complex layouts with alignment ```tsx // Before
Left
Right
 // After
Left
Right
 ``` ## Automated migration ### Using the codemod Run the codemod (available in v1.8.0): ```bash npx @optiaxiom/codemod flex-to-group src/ ``` The codemod will: - Transform `` → `` - Transform `` → `` - Transform `` → `` - Update imports: `import { Flex }` → `import { Group }` - Preserve all other props and children ## Manual migration ### Step-by-step checklist If you prefer to migrate manually, follow these steps: 1. **Import Group instead of Flex:** ```tsx // Before import { Flex } from "@optiaxiom/react"; // After import { Group } from "@optiaxiom/react"; ``` 2. **Update component usage:** - If you had no `flexDirection` prop: add `flexDirection="column" gap="16"` - If you had `flexDirection="row"`: remove it (that's the Group default) - If you had `flexDirection="column"`: keep it - If you had no `gap` prop: add `gap="16"` (or your desired gap) 3. **Test your changes:** - Verify layouts render correctly - Check responsive breakpoints still work - Ensure alignments are as expected ## Common patterns ### Form layouts ```tsx // Before // After ``` ### Button groups ```tsx // Before // After ``` ### Card content ```tsx // Before Title Description // After Title Description ``` ## Timeline ### Release schedule - **v1.8.0 (Current):** Group introduced, Flex deprecated, codemod available - **v2.0.0 (Future):** Flex removed, Group renamed to Flex with new defaults
